structured_data.title: The Intouchables
structured_data.description: Philippe, a wealthy quadriplegic, hires Driss, an ex-convict, as his caregiver. Despite cultural and social differences, the two form a deep friendship that transforms their lives. Through humor, empathy, and mutual respect, they navigate physical, emotional, and social challenges. The film explores friendship, personal growth, and human dignity, blending comedy and drama to highlight the transformative power of connection and understanding across divides.
structured_data.writer: Olivier Nakache, Éric Toledano, Philippe Pozzo di Borgo
structured_data.awards: Nominated for 1 BAFTA Award. 38 wins & 40 nominations total

community_snippets.title: Letterboxd review of The Intouchables
community_snippets.snippet: [Letterboxd Review of "The Intouchables"] I like to think that if this was released now, it would be torn apart by audiences, rather than just a few critics. I like to think it would be roundly rejected and would inspire frequent think pieces that were also full of recommendations of what you should watch instead.But then I remember Green Book won best picture and that this film’s overt popularity is because it gives the people what they want. It gives them the stereotype of Blackness they expect and parades it for their amusement while also promoting a world in which ‘we can all get along’. A world underpinned by harmful stereotypes
